Facials & your skincare routine

A facial appointment offers time to discuss your skin concerns and skincare routine. Learn what to ask about cleansing, exfoliation, hydration and home care before choosing a service.

A practical planning guide rewritten for this preview from the supplied website material. It is not medical advice or a clinically reviewed treatment recommendation.

Start with what you use at home

Bring a list of your current products and the concerns you want to discuss. A facial appointment is a chance to ask about cleansing, exfoliation, hydration and how a service fits your existing routine.

Understand the menu

A custom blend facial uses selected botanicals, solutions and masks. Microdermabrasion and dermaplaning are different forms of exfoliation. Ask the provider to explain the differences, suitability, preparation and aftercare rather than assuming every option is right for you.

Keep your expectations individual

Ask what a single appointment includes and what changes, if any, are realistic for your skin. Results vary. Persistent or concerning skin problems should be discussed with a qualified healthcare professional.

Plan your visit

Review published facial prices, then contact the spa to confirm current details and book. Let the team know about recent procedures and sensitivities before your visit.
